name: Satyr
summary: Across Kalimdor, satyr sects foul woodlands and moonwells. They began as Highborne night elves, transformed by Sargeras during the War of the Ancients. Now they torment their kaldorei kin and spread fel corruption in the Burning Legion’s name.

sections.title: Origins of the Curse
sections.body:
During the War of the Ancients, Xavius failed to hold the Burning Legion’s first gateway against Malfurion Stormrage. Sargeras tore apart the Highborne councilor’s spirit, then remade him as punishment and a tool. Xavius kept an elven torso but gained horns, taloned claws, a leonine tail, and a goat’s cloven lower body.

Sent back to Zin-Azshari, Xavius eagerly spread his fel affliction among other power-hungry Highborne. Xavius was struck down, but his demonic descendants survived. They still seek to make more of their kind by corrupting others.

sections.title: After the Sundering
sections.body: After the Great Sundering, surviving satyrs continued to threaten the shattered night elf civilization. Over the ages, they were broken and driven away. Their remnants split into scattered sects that linger in dark forests and ancient ruins, still hating their kaldorei cousins.

sections.title: Corrupters of Kalimdor
sections.body:
Satyr clans now dwell in deep woodland enclaves across Kalimdor, from Darkshore and Ashenvale to Felwood, Azshara, and Feralas. They feed on the land’s pure magic, leeching and spoiling nature until their hooves swell with drained arcane energy.

Satyrs turn peaceful furbolg tribes violent, taint ancient moonwells, and work as covert liaisons for the Shadow Council and the Burning Blade. Some join Twilight’s Hammer cultists or hide in ancient ruins such as Dire Maul. All remain bound to the Burning Legion’s shadow.

faq.answer: A satyr is a demon made from a night elf by an ancient fel curse. Satyrs have cloven hooves, horns, sharp claws, and a tail. Their elven torsos bear mastery of dark fel sorcery and physical savagery.

Lord Xavius, Highborne sorcerer and chief advisor to Queen Azshara, was the first satyr. He failed to defend the Burning Legion’s portal during the War of the Ancients. Sargeras then remade his body into a horned demon as punishment and a dark gift.

Yes. Satyrs can pass their transformative curse to other beings, chiefly night elves. The magic has weakened over the millennia, so successful transformations are far rarer now. Scattered cultists sometimes revere Xavius in hope of gaining the transformation.
Scattered reports speak of female satyrs, but no irrefutable proof of their existence has been secured.

faq.q: Why do satyrs target moonwells and forests?
faq.answer: Satyrs feed on purity and natural arcane magic, drawing it from pristine lands and night elf moonwells. The stolen energy gathers in their hooves, which swell and lose their cloven shape as they absorb immense magical power.

faq.q: Where are satyrs found right now?
faq.answer: Satyrs are scattered through ruined and corrupted reaches of Kalimdor: Satyrnaar and Xavian in Ashenvale, Bashal'Aran in Darkshore, Jadefire Run in Felwood, Sargeron in Desolace, the Haldarr and Legash encampments in Azshara, and Dire Maul in Feralas.

angles.text: As a night elf, you see satyrs as the ultimate betrayal of kaldorei heritage. They are a bitter reminder of the Highborne’s arrogance during the War of the Ancients.
As a druid, you know satyrs poison the wilds, corrupt furbolgs, and defile sacred groves. The Cenarion Circle sees their destruction as urgent.
As a warlock, you see the corruptive power of the Burning Legion’s ancient curses in satyrs. Their malice is demonic.
As an Alliance member, you fight alongside Sentinels to clear satyr camps encroaching on night elven settlements in Ashenvale and Darkshore.
As a member of the Horde, you clash with satyr sects in Ashenvale and Desolace. You root out their secret alliances with the Burning Blade.
